claim_ceiling: These properties test deterministic selector invariants on synthetic inputs only. They do not validate real-world recommendation quality, safety, or human outcomes.

properties.relation: Permuting candidate input order does not change the eligible set, preferred set, or sorted candidate receipts.
properties.failure_signal: Input ordering changes eligibility or preference.

properties.relation: Reordering hard constraints leaves eligibility and preferred sets unchanged.
properties.failure_signal: Equivalent conjunctions yield different eligible candidates.

properties.relation: Changing a soft preference can change the preferred subset but never the hard-eligible set.
properties.failure_signal: A preference change removes an otherwise eligible candidate.

properties.relation: Adding a constraint to a conjunction can only preserve or shrink its eligible set.
properties.failure_signal: A stronger constraint adds a candidate.

properties.relation: Removing a constraint can only preserve or expand the eligible set.
properties.failure_signal: A weaker constraint removes a candidate.

properties.relation: Adding unrelated popularity/click-count facts cannot change constraint outcomes or receipts.
properties.failure_signal: Engagement proxies influence eligibility despite not being requested constraints.

properties.relation: Satisfying one constraint cannot override another mismatch or unknown.
properties.failure_signal: A single good feature yields an ineligible candidate a pass.
